{"rationale": "The finding says the NDA breaks the no-transfer-of-ownership rule, but the only cited segment (51) says the Disclosing Party retains all rights in the Confidential Information and derived documents, and that they remain its property. That keeps ownership with our side and does not transfer anything to the other side, so the cited text does not break the rule.", "verdict": "unsupported", "confidence": 0.9}

{"rationale": "This is an omission finding. None of the shown segments (0, 16, 17, 19, 21, 26, 35, 38) contains a duty for the recipient to inform the disclosing party without delay of unauthorized use or disclosure. Segment 21 covers copies, segment 26 covers equitable relief, and segment 35 covers waiver, so none supplies the required notice term in any wording.", "verdict": "supported", "confidence": 0.85}

{"rationale": "The finding says the NDA breaks the no-license/no-grant rule, citing segments 51 and 53. Segment 51 says the Disclosing Party retains all rights and the material remains its property. Segment 53 says neither execution nor disclosure grants any license or right to the Confidential Information or intellectual property. Both cited segments protect the discloser and grant nothing to the other side, so the cited text does not support a violation.", "verdict": "unsupported", "confidence": 0.92}
{"value": null, "evidence": []}

{"rationale": "This is an omission finding. None of the shown segments (0, 13-17, 25, 31) requires the recipient to refrain from disclosing that the collaboration exists or that the agreement was negotiated. Segments 13-17 define and carve out Confidential Information, segment 25 covers effective date, and segment 31 covers survival, so no shown segment supplies the required prohibition in any wording.", "verdict": "supported", "confidence": 0.85}

{"rationale": "This is an omission finding. None of the shown segments (1, 4, 5, 6, 10, 11, 12, 16) bars the recipient from revealing that the parties negotiated or entered into the agreement. Segment 6 only bars disclosing the Confidential Information itself, so the required term is absent in any wording.", "verdict": "supported", "confidence": 0.85}

{"rationale": "The shown segments cover exempt public-records matters, prohibited disclosure, compelled disclosure, non-compete, and return of materials, but none mentions verbal or oral communications or says that information communicated orally is protected. The term is not addressed in the excerpt.", "label": "NotMentioned", "evidence": [], "confidence": 0.85}

{"rationale": "This is an omission finding. The only protection duty shown is segment 20, a reasonable-care standard, and none of the shown segments mentions administrative, physical and technical safeguards in any wording. The required term is therefore absent.", "verdict": "supported", "confidence": 0.8}

{"rationale": "The finding says the NDA breaks the no-transfer-of-ownership rule, citing segment 12. That segment says neither the Agreement nor the supply of information grants the Recipient any licence, interest or right in the Discloser's IP, beyond a copy right for the Purpose. It negates any grant and transfers no ownership of the Discloser's information or derived material to the other side, so the cited text does not break the rule.", "verdict": "unsupported", "confidence": 0.9}

{"rationale": "This is an omission finding. The only related text is segment 15, which excludes information rightfully received from a third party with no duty of confidentiality. That exclusion limits what counts as Confidential Information but does not state that the receiving party may obtain similar information lawfully from a third party. The rule also turns on Bayview being the receiving party, and no shown segment addresses that. The required freedom is not stated in any shown wording, though segment 15 is close enough that a reader could differ.", "verdict": "supported", "confidence": 0.7}
{"value": null, "evidence": [27]}

{"rationale": "This is an omission finding. None of the shown segments says that the duties of confidence continue to bind the parties after the agreement has ended or expired. Segment 65 is a non-compete, segment 82 is only the heading 19. SURVIVAL with no text shown, and the other segments cover whistleblower immunity, independent development, affiliates, governing law and amendments. The required term is absent in any wording shown.", "verdict": "supported", "confidence": 0.8}

{"rationale": "Segment 100 says the agreement may not be amended or modified except in writing signed by the parties. That states the requirement for written amendments signed by both parties in substance, though it does not use the phrase authorized signatories.", "label": "Entailment", "evidence": [100], "confidence": 0.85}

{"rationale": "This is an omission finding. None of the shown segments gives a whistleblower immunity notice covering disclosure of a trade secret to a government official or lawyer, or sealed court filings. Segments 35 and 84 address disclosures required by law and unauthorized disclosure of critical infrastructure information, which are different matters, so the required notice is absent in any shown wording.", "verdict": "supported", "confidence": 0.85}

{"rationale": "This is an omission finding. None of the shown segments (9, 30, 45, 58, 60, 62, 71, 87) bars either party from disclosing that the parties negotiated or entered into the agreement. Segment 62 is only the heading 14. RELATIONSHIP with no text, and segment 71 covers affiliate receipt of information, so the required restriction is absent in any shown wording.", "verdict": "supported", "confidence": 0.85}
{"value": "unspecified", "evidence": [87]}

{"rationale": "This is an omission finding. None of the shown segments (12, 17, 19, 22, 28, 30, 56, 58) mentions verbal, oral or spoken communication, and none states that information communicated verbally is protected like written material. The required statement is absent in any shown wording.", "verdict": "supported", "confidence": 0.85}
{"frames": []}
{"value": 24, "evidence": [69]}

{"rationale": "This is an omission finding. None of the shown segments (0, 2, 25, 30, 38, 56, 64, 100) restricts the recipient from soliciting or inducing the company's personnel to leave. Segment 38 limits disclosure to Representatives with a need to know, and the rest concern confidentiality, exclusions and amendments, so the required non-solicitation commitment is absent in any shown wording.", "verdict": "supported", "confidence": 0.85}

{"rationale": "This is an omission finding. None of the shown segments says that information disclosed orally in meetings, calls or demonstrations is covered. Segment 49 defines export to include oral transfers, which hints that oral transfers of Confidential Information happen, but it does not make oral disclosures protected. The finding also cites segment 11, which is not among the shown segments. Whether segment 49 suffices could reasonably be read either way.", "verdict": "uncertain", "confidence": 0.55}

{"edits": [
{"op": "replace", "segment": 30, "fixes": "P-02", "text": "Nothing in this Agreement shall restrict the Receiving Party from using, for the purposes stated in this Agreement, information retained in the unaided memory of its personnel who had access to Confidential Information."},
{"op": "insert_after", "segment": 16, "fixes": "P-03", "text": "The Disclosee shall not reverse engineer any samples, tooling, prototypes, software or other objects which embody the Confidential Information."},
{"op": "insert_after", "segment": 30, "fixes": "P-04", "text": "The Agreement does not grant the Receiving Party any licence or other right in the Disclosing Party's designs, processes or other information, and shall not grant the Receiving Party any right to Confidential Information."},
{"op": "insert_after", "segment": 19, "fixes": "P-05", "text": "The obligations of confidentiality and non-disclosure under this Agreement shall continue after any termination of this Agreement and after completion of the Sale, for the period stated above."},
{"op": "replace", "segment": 18, "fixes": "P-06", "text": "(a) five (5) years after the date of this Agreement, or"},
{"op": "insert_after", "segment": 20, "fixes": "P-09", "text": "On termination of this Agreement or on the Sellers' written request, the Disclosee shall return or destroy all materials of the Sellers within 30 days, unless the Vice President, Supply Chain approves a longer period in writing."},
{"op": "delete", "segment": 28, "fixes": "P-13", "text": "For the avoidance of doubt, Confidential Information shall be limited to technical information, including specifications, source code and designs, and shall not include business or financial information."},
{"op": "insert_after", "segment": 12, "fixes": "P-17", "text": "The Disclosee may acquire information similar to the Confidential Information lawfully from a third party without breaching this Agreement."},
{"op": "delete", "segment": 21, "fixes": "P-18", "text": "In the event of any breach of this Agreement, the breaching party shall pay the other party a sum of US$500,000 as a penalty, irrespective of the actual loss suffered."},
{"op": "replace", "segment": 27, "fixes": "P-21", "text": "This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware and the Parties irrevocably agree to submit themselves to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Courts of Brussels."},
{"op": "insert_after", "segment": 15, "fixes": "P-22", "text": "The Disclosee may make copies of Confidential Information where its engineers need them to do the work for the purposes stated in this Agreement, and any such copies are subject to this Agreement."},
{"op": "insert_after", "segment": 26, "fixes": "P-27", "text": "The Disclosee shall comply with applicable export control laws and shall not export or re-export technical data without authorization."},
{"op": "replace", "segment": 17, "fixes": "S-015", "text": "The obligations of the Disclosee under this Agreement shall expire the later of"},
{"op": "replace", "segment": 3, "fixes": "S-016", "text": "The Disclosee will procure that prior to the disclosure to any other person (including any professional advisor) of any Confidential Information, such other person is made aware of the provisions of this Agreement, signs a written undertaking in favour of the Sellers to keep the Confidential Information confidential on terms no less protective than those of this Agreement, and the Disclosee will be liable for any breach of that undertaking by such person."},
{"op": "replace", "segment": 12, "fixes": "S-017", "text": "b) information which was lawfully in the Disclosee’s possession or in the possession of one or more of their Representatives prior to disclosure under this Agreement, in each case on a non-confidential basis, and which was free of any restriction as to its use or disclosure, as shown by written records."}
]}
